description: The main objective of this project is to create an interactive space mission simulator where players are appointed as the captain of their own mission. In this game ,you will make critical decisions based on your knowledge of the cosmos and aerospace engineering. Through trial and error,players will quickly discover that space exploration involves critical thinking and great navigation.
summary:
Voyagers 2.0 is an interactive web platform that combines real NASA planetary mapping with a 2D landing flight simulator for the Moon and Mars. Named in honor of NASA’s Voyager 1 reaching 1 light-day from Earth, the project brings next-generation space exploration directly into any web browser.

We developed a two-part mission experience: first, users explore 2D and 3D planetary maps built with NASA Solar System Treks data—analyzing terrain elevation, surface temperature, radiation, solar lighting, and quake/impact hazards to choose a safe landing site. Second, users enter a 2D flight simulator where they pilot a lander to the surface, making real-time decisions on thrust, fuel management, and speed while adapting to lunar vacuum or thin Martian air.

Normally, planetary GIS datasets require complex scientific software, and static maps don't show how environmental hazards affect real spacecraft maneuvers. Voyagers 2.0 solves this by uniting real orbital data with hands-on decision-making, making space science accessible, engaging, and intuitive for students, educators, and future explorers.
details:
Voyagers 2.0 is a web app that combines interactive planetary maps of the Moon and Mars with a 2D landing flight simulator.

The Meaning Behind the Name

Our project is named Voyagers 2.0 in honor of NASA’s Voyager 1, which next week (November 2026) reaches the historic milestone of 1 light-day away from Earth—nearly 26 billion kilometers into interstellar space. Just as Voyager 1 pushed the boundaries of humanity's first deep-space reconnaissance, Voyagers 2.0 represents the next generation of exploration: turning real planetary data into an interactive tool where anyone can scout and land on new worlds.

What It Does & How It Works

  • Explore Real NASA Maps: Users can view 2D and 3D maps of the Moon and Mars using official NASA data layers—including terrain elevation, surface temperature, radiation levels, solar lighting, and quake/impact hazards—to find safe landing spots.
  • 2D Landing Flight Simulator: After choosing a target area, users enter a 2D flight simulator where they pilot a spacecraft down to the surface. Players make real-time decisions—controlling thrust, saving fuel, adjusting speed, and dodging rough terrain—to land safely on the Moon or Mars.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Makes Space Data Easy to Use: Normally, NASA planetary maps require complex scientific software. Voyagers 2.0 puts them in a simple web browser anyone can use.
  • Learn by Doing: Instead of just reading numbers on a map, users experience how gravity, thin Martian air, fuel limits, and steep craters affect a real landing.
  • Inspires STEM Learning: Helps students and space fans understand the real challenges of landing on other worlds in a fun, hands-on way.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Web App & Maps: React, TypeScript, JavaScript, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet (2D maps), and Three.js (3D globes).
  • 2D Flight Simulator & Audio: Godot 4 (WebGL export), HTML5 Canvas, and Web Audio API for thruster and HUD sound effects.
  • NASA Data: NASA Solar System Treks (LRO, MOLA, Diviner, THEMIS), NASA DONKI (space weather), and NASA PDS datasets.
  • Development Tools: Google AI Studio, Visual Studio Code, Vite, GitHub, and Canva.

How It Is Creative

Most space apps either show static maps or act as pure arcade games. Voyagers 2.0 connects both: you scout real NASA hazard maps first, and then test your landing skills in a 2D flight simulator shaped by those exact planetary conditions.

Key Factors Our Team Considered

  • Realistic Differences Between Worlds: Making sure landing on the airless Moon feels different from landing in Mars’s thin atmosphere.
  • Meaningful Player Choices: Designing the 2D simulator so every landing depends on smart fuel management and speed control.
  • Smooth Browser Performance: Keeping the maps, 3D views, and 2D simulator fast and responsive on normal laptops.
  • Clean Mission-Control Design: Organizing complex NASA data and flight controls into a simple, easy-to-read interface with toggleable audio.
